correctness.rationale: Completing the square gives the exact quartic factorization printed in RESULT.md and recovers the positive-horizontal-coordinate oval. Its vertical branch difference gives the genuine Euclidean area integral. The scaled-coordinate and trigonometric substitutions reduce the integral to complete elliptic integrals. Strictly nested horizontal slices prove area monotonicity. The NIST DLMF elliptic expansions retain the finite correction \(-1-\log16\) with a proved \(O(a|\log a|)\) remainder. The exact shear-adjusted normalization at \(a=1/4\) proves the disk limit and coefficient \(4\sqrt2\pi\). All hypotheses and normalization are explicit. A polynomial cofactor identity was checked symbolically, and high-precision independent quadrature was reproduced; these calculations supplement but do not replace the universal proof.

value.rationale: The area enclosed by an isolated periodic oval is a natural physical phase-plane geometric invariant, not an arbitrary parameter slice. A strict global area-to-parameter bijection and two exact, geometrically dissimilar degeneration laws expose the size and shape of the distinguished periodic boundary beyond qualitative phase portraits. The logarithmic finite part \(-1-\log16\) is nontrivial and determined without arbitrary fitting; no new broad theorem is claimed.
